newsitem.title: CANADA: Nortel CEO sees 15-20 pct sales growth.
newsitem.headline: Nortel CEO sees 15-20 pct sales growth.

text.p: Northern Telecom Ltd Chief Executive Jean Monty said on Tuesday the company's revenues should grow by 15 to 20 percent in 1997.

"We still maintain that we can meet our targets and that the revenue growth will be in the minimum mid-teens. So it's probably going to be between the 15 and 20 percent range," Monty said in a telephone interview.

He said Nortel's balance sheet looked solid in the first quarter and added that the company should soon announce the sale of customer financing debt, including the US$1.2 billion vendor financing of the Sprint Corp wireless contract.

"The balance sheet remains very strong with a low debt ratio at 26 percent. We will announce pretty soon the layoff of major customer financings, which will give us even more dry powder for the longer term in terms of doing more business," Monty said.
"(The Sprint deal) is done. We're going to announce that in the next couple of weeks," he added.
Monty said the long delay in getting the financing deal done was due to its complexity.
"It's a billion dollar deal," he said.
"And what's interesting about that is when you compare that to Lucent (Technologies Inc's) growth...they showed their growth in the U.S. market for operators at around 21 percent," Monty said.
Nortel's earnings per share were US$0.41 versus US$0.32 in the prior year period. Monty said he was pleased with the growth rate given that it was paired with strong sales growth.

"So earnings, after-tax margins, remained solid at the same level as last year even in the face of significant growth in revenues. Usually when you grow your busines that fast, you can see some softening of margins," Monty said.
